name: Neuro-cranial restructuring (NCR)

lead: Neuro-cranial restructuring (NCR) is an alternative therapy in which a small balloon (a finger cot on a tube) is inserted into the nasal passages and inflated briefly. Proponents say the pressure moves cranial bones such as the sphenoid and vomer, improving symmetry, facial structure, posture, breathing and headaches.

On looksmax.org it is discussed as a do-it-yourself bone-structure method. No published clinical studies have tested NCR for facial appearance, and the claim that adult skull bones can be reshaped this way has not been demonstrated in research.

paras: Forum guides describe a home-built device made from a blood-pressure bulb, a finger cot, dental floss and lubricant, inflated one nostril at a time until a sense of expansion is felt across the face. Practitioners and online guides also describe sessions with a trained provider.

The nasal cavity sits close to the skull base, sinuses and eyes. No published research has assessed the safety of NCR. Concerns raised in online guides include the risk of inhaling parts of the device.

angle.text: Proponents use NCR in the hope of correcting asymmetry or a tilted sphenoid and improving cranial structure. This is a claimed mechanism that published research has not tested.

lead: Neuro-cranial restructuring (NCR) is an alternative therapy that uses an inflatable balloon placed in the nasal passages. Its proponents say that repeated brief inflation transmits pressure to the sphenoid, vomer and other cranial bones and gradually changes their position.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities it appears under the bonehacks and fringe categories as a way to improve facial symmetry and cranial structure without surgery. A looksmax.org guide lists claimed benefits of improved symmetry and cranial structure, better posture and breathing, and less headache and tightness, and describes a home-built device.[1]
No clinical studies on NCR for facial shape have been published.
infobox: Inflatable intranasal balloon (finger cot, tube, bulb)

paras: NCR involves an inflatable balloon that is inserted into the nostril, inflated briefly, then released, usually in several passes on each side. Proponents describe a sensation of expansion extending through the face and into the opposite side as the goal of each inflation.[1]

The looksmax.org guide describes making the device at home: a sphygmomanometer bulb with a release valve, a finger cot, waxed dental floss to secure it and a lubricant such as aloe gel or water. It lists reduced risk of inhaling the balloon as a design consideration.[1]

The guide lists the claimed benefits as improved facial symmetry, cranial structure, posture, airway and fewer headaches.[1] In the replies, one user asks whether the method is used to fix a tilted sphenoid, described there as a main cause of asymmetry.[1]
Proponents therefore frame NCR as a non-surgical route to facial bone change, similar in intent to other bone-focused practices in the community.
The device sits in the nasal cavity near the sinuses, orbits and skull base. NCR is not an approved medical treatment, and no published research has assessed its safety or effects.

lore.intro: NCR is discussed on looksmax.org as a full do-it-yourself guide, with replies that bookmark it or ask about its mechanism.[1]
